options.text: The Supreme Court reversed the decision within one year
Georgia voluntarily repealed all of its laws affecting the Cherokee
The Cherokee Nation agreed to accept Georgia’s authority over its territory

rationales.A: Background: President Andrew Jackson declined to enforce federal protection for the Cherokee, so the legal victory did not prevent removal.
rationales.B: The decision was not reversed within one year.
rationales.C: Georgia did not repeal its laws affecting the Cherokee.
rationales.D: The Cherokee did not accept Georgia's authority over its territory.
rationales.general:
1. Note the gap. The Court ruled for the Cherokee, yet removal went ahead.
2. Ask who had to act. Background: Jackson declined to use federal power to protect the Cherokee.
3. Test the other explanations. No reversal, no repeal, and no Cherokee acceptance occurred.
4. Connect the inaction to the outcome. A ruling without enforcement had limited practical effect.
Remember: a court decision matters only as far as someone enforces it.

source: original; stimulus is a verbatim public-domain excerpt from Worcester v. Georgia (1832) with the 1836 Topographical Bureau removal map
stem: Which of the following most directly explains why the *Worcester* decision had limited practical effect in the 1830s?

stimulus.source_note: Worcester v. Georgia, 1832, majority opinion by Chief Justice John Marshall, public domain. Map: Topographical Bureau, 1836, Library of Congress.
stimulus.text: “The Cherokee Nation . . . are . . . a distinct community, occupying its own territory . . . in which the laws of Georgia can have no force . . . The Acts of Georgia are repugnant to the Constitution, laws, and treaties of the United States.”
